ai.description: *Amolops jaunsari* is a medium-sized frog with a brown, mottled dorsum and pale yellow belly. It features prominent, expanded toe discs and a distinct, dark lateral band extending from the snout to flanks.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Amolops jaunsari* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous white line along the upper lip, which is absent in most other similar Indian *Amolops* species.
ai.habitat: *Amolops jaunsari* inhabits fast-flowing, rocky mountain streams within moist temperate forests of the Western Himalayas, typically at elevations between 1,500 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Amolops jaunsari is a nocturnal frog that thrives in fast-flowing mountain streams, where it uses its specialized toe pads to cling to slippery, spray-drenched rocks.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Amolops jaunsari* is an oviparous species that breeds during the monsoon season, laying eggs in aquatic environments, though specific clutch size data remains limited.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Amolops jaunsari* is endemic to the Western Himalayas, specifically occurring in the Jaunsar-Bawar region of Uttarakhand, India, at elevations around 1,500–2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Jaunsar Stream Frog emits a series of high-pitched, rhythmic chirps that cut through the loud, constant roar of fast-flowing mountain streams in its Himalayan habitat.
